reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a purported way to obtain a high-value or free Uber ride code through an external generator and directs viewers to enter an email and complete verification tasks. The sampled pages connect the free-ride claim to a code-generation prompt and then to human verification or a survey step. The evidence does not establish that any code was delivered or redeemed.

citations.quote: How you can travel free in Uber Caps Free
today I will do a guide the new promo codes
which will make you get free ride using uber app
you will get a chance to generate promo code of hundreds of dollar
Here you need to add your email

opening.argument: The material uses the language of a promotional code and discount rather than a promise of guaranteed cash: it says promo codes can provide “cashback & discount.” The speaker also presents the process as something viewers may try, while the supplied evidence does not establish a payment, loss, or successful redemption. A careful reading therefore treats this as an ordinary promotion whose effectiveness and terms require independent verification, not as proof of deception.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the external generator, email field, and verification tasks as conclusive. Those details establish only that the advertised process had steps; they do not establish that viewers were charged, that data was misused, or that the offer could not work. The record also does not establish a successful or failed outcome.

citations.quote: Here you need to add your email
To get the code I have to do a task

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The affirmative claims are stronger than a neutral warning: the speaker says the site can generate a code worth hundreds of dollars and directs viewers through verification. The evidence therefore shows a purported benefit tied to a lead-generation flow, while the absence of a documented loss does not make the promotion non-deceptive.

citations.quote: you will get a chance to generate promo code of hundreds of dollar
finally you will be able to complete the task under minimum 5 mins

opening.argument: The video's stated format is instructional: the speaker says, “today I will do a guide,” explains where to obtain a code, and then explains where a coupon code is entered. It also presents the speaker's claimed prior use as an example for viewers. That is consistent with a how-to demonstration of an app-related process, even if viewers should independently assess whether the external site and code work.

then you will know where to put the codes you have to
with the help of a particular site www.uberapp.icu with its help i have taken uber rides for free

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the video a tutorial does not determine whether its central instructions are deceptive, but the prosecution still has to show more than an instructional format and an external website. The speaker describes the steps, demonstrates a code-entry context, and reports personal experience; those are features of a practical walkthrough, not independently proof of a scam.

citations.quote: then you will know where to put the codes you have to
now this code is invalid because im writing the code randomly

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial framing does not neutralize the substance of the instructions. The speaker explicitly claims the site will generate a high-value code, asks for an email, and says tasks must be completed before verification. A demonstration of a process can still promote a deceptive process, and no working code or Uber redemption is shown.

citations.quote: you will get a chance to generate promo code of hundreds of dollar
To verify the code I have to do few tasks

opening.argument: The subject is an ordinary service promotion: the title identifies an Uber free-ride code, and the narration describes promo codes, cashback, and discounts. The sampled Uber payment screen shows Cash selected, rather than an investment, deposit, or promised financial return. The supplied material shows no downline income, investment opportunity, or guaranteed return; it presents a claimed coupon flow that may be evaluated like other promotional offers.

citations.quote: Uber free ride code 2019 #uberride #freeridecode
basically it gets some promo codes we get cashback & discount from them

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution infers scam status from the use of an external page and verification step, but those are not the same as a deposit, investment, or guaranteed-return mechanism. The evidence does not show a charge, financial loss, or unusable ride. At most, it shows a promotional flow whose relationship to Uber requires checking.

citations.quote: To get the code I have to do a task
I have bought Uber rights free of cost

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The missing investment features are beside the point because this category concerns low-barrier acquisition of a purported benefit. The video directs viewers to an external generator, requests an email, and conditions the code on verification tasks. Its claim of having obtained free rides is only the speaker's assertion; no functioning code or redemption is established.
